headline: P0215 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share of 32.7% vs 5.2% expected for its patient mix, elevated in every complexity stratum and most sharply on low-complexity patients
rationale: P0215 billed 817 of 2,500 claims as 99215 (32.7%). Given its patients' complexity, the expected share is 5.2% (z vs peers 4.18, risk-adjusted score 22.7). A sicker panel does not explain the gap. The excess shows up in every stratum and is largest where acuity is lowest. For patients with 0 chronic conditions the provider's 99215 share is 18.0% vs 2.1% for all providers (about 8.6x). For 1 condition it is 25.4% vs 3.4% (about 7.5x). For 5+ conditions it is 48.5% vs 29.8% (about 1.6x). In the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, many visits have a single minor diagnosis code. Examples are rash R21 (C0098191, C0098499, C0098788, C0099738), upper respiratory infection J06.9 (C0098773, C0099737, C0099825), UTI N39.0 (C0098522) and low back pain M54.50 in a 23-year-old (C0097623). By contrast, comparison claim C0097804 is a 0-condition J06.9 visit billed 99213. The sampled high-complexity 99215s look plausible, for example C0099387 (6 conditions, age 92) and C0097886. Together this is consistent with upcoding, not a high-acuity panel. However, the claim lists are random samples, and there is no clinical documentation, time or MDM detail, so medical necessity cannot be judged from this packet.
next_steps: Request full medical records (MDM documentation and/or total time) for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with the single-diagnosis R21, J06.9, N39.0 and M54.50 visits.
Draw a statistically valid random sample of the provider's 99215 claims across all strata for coding review, and extrapolate only from that.
Check whether time-based coding, prolonged services or telehealth explain the high levels, and whether a template or EHR default drives the 99215 selection.
Compare the 99215 rates of individual rendering clinicians within the practice, and look at trends over time in 2024.
Check for any prior education, audits or payer edits related to E/M leveling for this provider.
